records.quote:
Suddenly,
he slammed it to the ground. The paint chipped and cracked. The small
head rolled loosely across the lawn.
records.paraphrase: The Secretary, disturbed by his role, smashes one of Brandon's puppets on the ground.

records.quote:
The Government was ubiquitous,
omnipresent and omnipotent. It dominated every conversation, every
business, every life from birth to death.
records.paraphrase: The story's world features an all-encompassing government that controls every aspect of life.

records.quote:
If the sole
purpose of the government is to serve the taxpayers--and there were no
more--how could we justify our existence in office?
records.paraphrase: The President reasons that if no taxpayers remained, the government would have no justification to exist.

records.quote:
Calculators and computers adjust our
salary each year in proportion to the expense of the government. We
have been operating out of the red that way for years.
records.paraphrase: Government employee salaries are automatically adjusted by computers to match government expenses, keeping the budget balanced.

records.quote:
For the first time it
was clear to him why he had been so reluctant to give up his work.
records.paraphrase: Brandon suddenly realizes why he has resisted giving up his puppet-making work.

records.quote:
After all, the government
works for the taxpayers, Evans--and Brandon is the last taxpayer. He's
our boss, son. The only boss we have left.
records.paraphrase: The President reverses expected power relations, concluding that the lone remaining taxpayer is the government's true boss.

records.quote:
They had
known Brandon was a stubborn man, that was why things were done as they
were. The offering of worthless positions had been a feint. He should
have grabbed at something he could handle. And the tax forms! That was
supposed to be the last straw. They had been loaded, prepared just for
Brandon, to break his resistence.
records.paraphrase: The government deliberately engineered worthless job offers and loaded tax forms as a calculated strategy to break Brandon's resistance.

records.quote:
Government employees never do. We are paid a flat sum and our
subsistance is taken care of.
records.paraphrase: Government employees never file taxes; they receive a flat salary with subsistence provided.

records.quote:
One hundred days!" Evans laughed. "Soon it'll be every day of the
year. Then where will you be?" He looked directly into Brandon's eyes.
"Can't you see? You're in the web already, working a third of the year
without compensation.
records.paraphrase: The growing complexity of tax forms consumes ever more of Brandon's year, portrayed as an inescapable trap.

records.quote:
Brandon was the last taxpayer. We've
been forced to operate an entire bureau just to process his forms. It's
the only department operating in the red.
records.paraphrase: Because Brandon is the sole remaining taxpayer, an entire government bureau exists only to process his forms and runs at a loss.

records.quote:
He's the only person not
employed by the government, the only one still operating a private
business!
records.paraphrase: In this society everyone except Brandon is employed by the government, and he alone runs a private business.

criteria.rationale: The story is a social-political satire; no scientific fact, theory, discovery, or natural process is materially represented. Mention of calculators/computers is incidental and not a scientific idea.

Computers automatically adjusting government salaries to keep the budget balanced is an engineered system in the setting, but it functions as background world-building rather than a decisive invention driving the plot; interpretation of its materiality is uncertain.

The story is set in a speculative future society where a total government employs everyone except one man, but no explicit temporal markers or displacement anchor it firmly; the futurity is implied rather than stated.

The story systematically extrapolates from the premise of an ever-expanding government: everyone becomes a government employee, only one taxpayer remains, an entire bureau runs at a loss to process his forms, and the government's very justification collapses. This consequence-development is the core of the story.

The government engineers a deliberate psychological strategy (loaded forms, feint offers) to break Brandon, and Evans is described as a psychologist testing tactics; this resembles hypothesis-and-manipulation but is closer to scheming than systematic scientific inference driving understanding.
No other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them appear; the setting is an ordinary terrestrial estate near a city.

No large-scale natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused disaster is actual, impending, remembered, or causally central. The crisis is administrative and satirical, not catastrophic in scale.

candidates.description: A near-future society in which the government has become ubiquitous, omnipresent, and omnipotent, employing essentially every person and controlling every business and every life from birth to death, with a self-balancing salary system that eliminates traditional taxation for its (universal) workforce.

novelty.rationale: The story posits a totalizing social order that differs categorically from the implied empirical norm: a government that has absorbed the entire population as employees, so that only one private citizen and one taxpayer remains. This is a world-altering difference in social organization, not a mere gadget.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The premise is developed as a coherent, immanent socioeconomic system: employees are paid flat sums with subsistence provided, computers adjust salaries to government expense to stay out of the red, and the bureaucracy deliberately engineers loaded tax forms and worthless job offers as calculated pressure. It is a systematic imaginary social organization with no supernatural element.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The entire plot and its ironic reversal derive from this novum: the government's obsessive campaign to recruit Brandon exists solely because he is the last taxpayer, and the closing revelation that the last taxpayer is the government's true boss and its sole justification for existing is the governing logic of the whole story.

estrangement.rationale:
The estranging inversion of expected power relations
dthe realization that an all-powerful government logically depends on and serves its single remaining taxpayer
dforces the reader to reconsider the ostensible purpose of government, a cognitively estranging contrast with the empirical norm.

candidates.description: Brandon's revival of the almost-lost art of hand-carved puppets, which have become world famous.

novelty.rationale: Hand-carved puppets are an ordinary craft object within the empirical norm; they represent an anachronistic individual pursuit rather than a totalizing, world-altering difference. They function as a thematic symbol of individual creative autonomy, not as a novum.

cognitive_validation.rationale: No imaginary science or systematic novel logic attaches to the puppets; there is nothing to validate cognitively because they are mundane.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The puppets are a recurring symbolic motif and emotional anchor, but the narrative logic is governed by the total-government/last-taxpayer premise, not by the puppets themselves. They are an incidental (if meaningful) device.

estrangement.rationale: The puppets provide symbolic contrast between individual creativity and bureaucratic conformity, but they do not themselves generate cognitive estrangement of the storyworld.
